chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I first entered upon him, he said: Learn truthfulness before learning the Hadith.'
ai.seo_question: Why should one learn truthfulness before studying Hadith?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes that moral integrity (sidq) is a prerequisite for authentic knowledge transmission, distinguishing true scholars from those who merely narrate. This instruction underscores the Shia scholarly tradition that the reliability of a narrator (thiqa) is rooted in their truthfulness in speech and action, ensuring the purity of the transmitted message. It serves as a critical methodological principle for verifying the chain of transmission and the character of the scholar.
